title: Ordering-Aware Theory of Trotter Error
authors: Zhenning Liu, Zhi-Yuan Wei, Michael Foss-Feig, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Andrew M. Childs
abstract: Product formulas are a basic tool for simulating quantum many-body dynamics, but a fundamental degree of freedom in their application---the ordering of Hamiltonian terms---has remained largely unexplored. Here we systematically study such ordering effects, quantifying their impact on simulation accuracy and exploiting them to design more accurate product-formula simulations. We develop an efficiently computable, ordering-sensitive bound on the finite-step-size Trotter error for geometrically local Hamiltonians for arbitrarily high-order product formulas. For translation-invariant one-dimensional chains, our bounds are close to exact second-, fourth-, and sixth-order Trotter errors in small-system tests, while on large-scale systems they improve on previous higher-order analytical bounds by orders of magnitude. We further use the local structure of the error bounds and estimates to optimize ordering efficiently, reducing the long-chain problem to a minimum-mean-weight-cycle problem on a weighted de Bruijn graph. For random translation-invariant chains, sequential (staircase-like) orderings consistently outperform standard brickwall circuits; when circuit depth is restricted, the optimizer instead favors wave-like parallel-sequential orderings, which preserve much of the accuracy advantage over brickwall circuits. These results establish ordering as a useful degree of freedom for both understanding and improving product-formula simulation.
summary: This paper introduces an ordering-aware theory to analyze and improve the accuracy of Trotterization for simulating quantum many-body dynamics. By quantifying how the sequence of Hamiltonian terms affects the error bound, the authors show that specific orderings, like sequential or wave-like, yield significantly more accurate simulations than standard methods. This establishes term ordering as a critical, exploitable degree of freedom in quantum simulation.
main_problem: The paper systematically studies the impact of the ordering of Hamiltonian terms on the accuracy of product-formula simulations (Trotterization) for quantum many-body dynamics.
main_result: The authors developed an ordering-sensitive bound on the Trotter error that is nearly optimal, showing that sequential or wave-like orderings significantly outperform standard brickwall circuits.
method: They develop an efficiently computable, ordering-sensitive bound on the finite-step-size Trotter error by organizing error contributions by spatial support and employing graph-theoretic algorithms to optimize the term ordering.
model_or_system: The study focuses on simulating the time evolution of quantum many-body systems governed by geometrically local, translation-invariant Hamiltonians, initially on 1D nearest-neighbor chains.
key_observables: Trotter Error, Optimality Ratio, Mean Optimality Ratios.
important_parameters: Product formula order ($p=2, 4, 6$), step size ($	au$), chain length ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on 1D translation-invariant nearest-neighbor Hamiltonians, and the error bound is derived from the nondegenerate part of the leading-order error.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate different term orderings (e.g., brickwall vs. sequential) and compare Trotter errors for various models, while later figures compare performance metrics like the optimality ratio across different optimization strategies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the core problem—the role of ordering—to developing the error bound based on spatial support, optimizing the ordering using de Bruijn graphs, and finally validating the findings by comparing sequential, wave-like, and brickwall orderings on random chains.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial theoretical tools for improving the efficiency and accuracy of quantum simulation algorithms, directly impacting how quantum dynamics are modeled in quantum computing and AMO physics.
